'''Armed conflicts and attacks'''
*[[Afghanistan conflict (1978–present)|Afghanistan conflict]]
**[[Islamic State–Taliban conflict]]
***[[Taliban]] soldiers raid an [[Islamic State – Khorasan Province|IS–K]] hideout in [[Kabul]], arresting four [[militant]]s. Meanwhile, [[Islamic State of Iraq and the Levant|ISIL]] claims responsibility for the [[Decapitation|beheading]] of a Taliban soldier in [[Jalalabad]]. [https://www.reuters.com/world/asia-pacific/taliban-say-four-islamic-state-members-captured-near-kabul-2021-10-06/ (Reuters)]
*[[Nigerian bandit conflict]]
**Dozens of armed [[bandit]]s on motorbikes storm a village in [[Zamfara]], killing 18 civilians, burning shops and cars, and forcing many residents to flee. [https://www.reuters.com/world/africa/armed-bandits-kill-18-nigerias-zamfara-state-2021-10-06/ (Reuters)]
*[[Mali War]]
**A battle between [[jihadism|jihadists]] and [[Malian Armed Forces|Malian forces]] in the central [[Mopti Region]] leaves at least nine soldiers and 15 [[insurgent]]s dead. The mayor of the nearby town of [[Bankass]] says that up to 16 soldiers were killed in the attack. [https://www.reuters.com/world/africa/islamist-militant-attack-kills-least-five-mali-soldiers-toll-could-rise-2021-10-06/ (Reuters)]

'''Arts and culture'''
*The [[Afghanistan]] pavilion opens at the [[Expo 2020]] after being closed during the first week of the event following the [[2021 Taliban offensive|Taliban takeover]] in the country. [https://www.khaleejtimes.com/uae/expo-2020-dubai/expo-2020-dubai-afghanistan-pavilion-opens-to-visitors-rare-artefacts-on-display (''Khaleej Times'')]

'''Health and environment'''
*[[COVID-19 pandemic]]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Europe]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Denmark]], [[COVID-19 vaccination in Denmark]]
****[[Denmark]] suspends the use of the [[Moderna COVID-19 vaccine]] for people under the age of 18 after reports of [[myocarditis]] and [[meningitis]], which are rare side effects of the vaccine. [https://www.thelocal.dk/20211006/denmark-stops-offering-moderna-covid-19-vaccine-to-under-18s/ (''The Local Denmark'')]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Romania]]
****[[Romania]] reports a record 331 [[COVID-19 pandemic deaths|deaths]] from [[COVID-19]] in the past 24 hours, thereby bringing the nationwide death toll to 38,260. [https://www.euractiv.com/section/politics/short_news/romanias-covid-19-death-toll-hits-new-record/ (''Euractiv'')]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Russia]]
****[[Russia]] reports a record 929 [[COVID-19 pandemic deaths|deaths]] from COVID-19 in the past 24 hours, thereby bringing the nationwide death toll to 212,685. [https://gulfnews.com/world/europe/covid-19-russia-reports-record-929-deaths-in-a-day-1.82773106 (''Gulf News'')]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Sweden]], [[COVID-19 vaccination in Sweden]]
****[[Sweden]] temporarily suspends the use of the Moderna COVID-19 vaccine for people born since 1991 for precautionary reasons after reports of possible rare side effects, such as myocarditis. [https://www.cbsnews.com/news/covid-vaccine-moderna-sweden-halts-use-in-under-30s/ (CBS News)]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Asia]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Kazakhstan]]
****[[Kazakhstan]] signs an agreement to purchase four million doses of the [[Pfizer–BioNTech COVID-19 vaccine]] which will be delivered in the fourth quarter of this year. [https://lenta.inform.kz/kz/kazakhstan-expects-4-mln-doses-of-pfizer-covid-19-vaccine_a3845582 (KAZINFORM)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Singapore]]
****[[Singapore]] reports a record 3,577 new cases of COVID-19 in the past 24 hours, thereby bringing the nationwide total of confirmed cases to 113,381. [https://www.todayonline.com/singapore/covid-19-3577-new-cases-singapore-rise-number-patients-icu-need-oxygen-support (''TODAY'')]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Vietnam]]
****[[Vietnam]] surpasses 20,000 deaths from COVID-19. [https://e.vnexpress.net/news/news/vietnam-confirms-4-356-new-covid-19-cases-4368198.html (''VnExpress'')]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Brazil]], [[Travel restrictions related to the COVID-19 pandemic]]
***[[Brazil]] lifts an air travel restriction that prevented travel from the [[United Kingdom]], [[South Africa]] and [[India]] due to the pandemic. Travellers from these countries can now enter Brazil after showing a negative [[COVID-19 test]] result. [https://www.reuters.com/article/health-coronavirus-brazil-travelers/brazil-clears-travelers-from-the-uk-south-africa-and-india-to-enter-the-country-idUSL1N2R21OX (Reuters)]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Canada]], [[COVID-19 vaccination in Canada]]
***[[Canada|Canadian]] [[Government of Canada|federal government]] announces a nationwide COVID-19 vaccine mandate for rail and train passengers and will place unvaccinated core federal employees under unpaid leave as early as November 15 if they had not disclose their vaccination status by October 29. [https://www.cnn.com/travel/article/canada-trudeau-vaccine-mandate/index.html (CNN)]
*The [[World Health Organization]] endorses the mass rollout of the [[malaria vaccine]] [[RTS,S]] across [[Sub-Saharan Africa]] and other countries affected by the disease after pilot programs with the vaccine in [[Ghana]], [[Kenya]], and [[Malawi]] reduced malaria-related hospitalization and death rates among children by 70%. [https://www.theguardian.com/global-development/2021/oct/06/who-endorses-use-of-worlds-first-malaria-vaccine-in-africa (''The Guardian'')]

'''International relations'''
*[[Nuclear weapons of the United States]]
**The [[United States|U.S.]] [[United States Department of State|State Department]] reveals that the current stockpile of nuclear weapons is 3,750 warheads. [https://www.state.gov/transparency-in-the-u-s-nuclear-weapons-stockpile/ (State.gov)]
*[[Russia–NATO relations]]
**[[NATO]] expels eight members of the [[Russia–NATO relations|Russian Mission to NATO]], accusing the [[Russians]] of secretly operating as intelligence officers. NATO also reduces the number of Russian positions at the organization to 10. [https://www.military.com/daily-news/2021/10/06/nato-expels-8-undeclared-russian-intelligence-officers.html (Military.com)]
*[[Paris Agreement]]
**[[Turkey]] ratifies the Paris Climate Accords, an international treaty on [[climate change]], becoming the last [[G20]] country to do so. [https://www.msn.com/en-us/news/world/turkey-ratifies-paris-climate-agreement-last-g20-country-to-do-so/ar-AAPdfgq (MSN)]

'''Law and crime'''
*[[Abortion in the United States]]
**[[United States federal judge]] [[Robert L. Pitman]] issues an order to block the [[Texas Heartbeat Act]]. [https://www.usatoday.com/story/news/nation/2021/10/06/federal-judge-blocks-texas-restrictive-abortion-law/6030311001/ ''(USA Today)'']
*Four people are wounded as a gunman [[school shooting|opens fire at a high school]] in [[Arlington, Texas]], [[United States]] after a fight. The suspected attacker escaped from the scene, but was arrested several hours later. [https://www.thedailybeast.com/multiple-victims-reported-after-shooting-at-mansfield-timberview-high-school-arlington-texas (''The Daily Beast'')]
*[[Chile]]an opposition politicians agree to seek [[impeachment]] of [[President of Chile|President]] [[Sebastián Piñera]] due to potential conflict of interest and tax evasion, as revealed by the [[Pandora Papers]] which were released on Sunday. [https://en.mercopress.com/2021/10/06/chilean-opposition-agree-to-seek-pinera-s-impeachment-in-view-of-pandora-papers (Mercopress)]
*Case Breakers, a group of former law enforcement individuals, claim to have identified the [[Zodiac Killer]] as Gary Francis Poste, an individual who had passed away in 2018. The finding is vehemently disavowed by the [[FBI]], who assert the case is "still very much open". [https://www.independent.co.uk/news/world/americas/crime/zodiac-killer-identity-gary-poste-b1933514.html (''The Independent'')]

'''Politics and elections'''
*[[President of Peru|Peruvian President]] [[Pedro Castillo]] announces the resignation of [[Prime Minister of Peru|Prime Minister]] [[Guido Bellido]]. [[Mirtha Vásquez]] is sworn-in to replace Bellido. [https://www.reuters.com/world/americas/perus-castillo-says-pm-has-resigned-two-months-into-his-administration-2021-10-06/ (Reuters)] [https://andina.pe/INgles/noticia-peru-president-accepts-prime-ministers-resignation-864557.aspx (Andina)]

'''Science and technology'''
*[[Facebook Files]]
**[[Frances Haugen]], a former [[Facebook]] employee, tells U.S. lawmakers that the company's sites and apps "harm children, stoke division and weaken our democracy". [https://www.bbc.com/news/world-us-canada-58805965 (BBC News)]
*Chemists [[Benjamin List]] of [[Germany]] and [[David MacMillan]] of the [[United States]] are awarded the 2021 [[Nobel Prize in Chemistry]] for their work on [[molecular engineering]] through [[organocatalysis]]. [https://gulfnews.com/world/europe/german-benjamin-list-and-american-david-macmillan-win-nobel-chemistry-prize-1.82766399 (AFP via ''Gulf News'')]
